## Policies

### Peer Review

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Type** | Single-blind: "This journal follows a single-blind reviewing procedure" (https://link.springer.com/journal/799/submission-guidelines, read 2026-11-23). Author names and affiliations go on the title page |
| **Transferable / Cascade?** | Blank. No source on the pages read |
| **Reviewer reports published?** | Not stated on the guidelines page. Springer's preprint policy page describes an optional "In Review" service where some journals' authors can share peer-review information publicly; whether this journal takes part was not stated (https://www.springer.com/gp/editorial-policies/preprint-sharing, read 2026-11-23) |
| **Typical R+R rounds** | Blank. SciRev, 1 review: 2.0 rounds (https://scirev.org/journal/international-journal-on-digital-libraries/) |
| **Reviewer recommendations** | Authors are welcome to suggest suitable reviewers and ask to exclude some; authors should make sure suggested reviewers are totally independent, a mix of countries and institutions is recommended, and the corresponding author must provide an institutional e-mail address for each suggested reviewer or another means of verifying identity; the journal may not use the suggestions (guidelines page, read 2026-11-23) |

### AI Policy

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Has journal-specific AI policy?** | The journal's guidelines page carries the publisher's text; no bespoke journal rule was found (https://link.springer.com/journal/799/submission-guidelines, read 2026-11-23) |
| **Explicit permission gate?** | No gate. The page says use of a large language model "should be properly documented" in the Methods section (or a suitable alternative part) |
| **Leniency (1-5)** | 3 (this pass's own rubric: allowed with documentation expected (the page says "should") = 3; AI-assisted copy-editing needs no declaration) |
| **Summary** | Large language models do not satisfy authorship criteria. LLM use is documented in the Methods. "AI assisted copy editing" (improving readability, grammar, spelling, punctuation and tone of human-generated text, without generative editorial work or autonomous content creation) need not be declared. There must be human accountability for the final text. Retrieved 2026-11-23 |
| **Source URL** | https://link.springer.com/journal/799/submission-guidelines |

### Preprint Policy

> Publisher-level policy (Springer Nature), not journal-specific: the journal's own guidelines page does not mention preprints. Sources: https://www.springer.com/gp/editorial-policies/preprint-sharing and https://www.springernature.com/gp/open-research/policies/journal-policies, both read 2026-11-23.

| Stage | Allowed? | Notes |
|-------|----------|-------|
| Pre-submission | Yes | Springer Nature journals encourage posting preprints of primary research manuscripts on servers of the author's choice or the author's or an institutional website; posting is not prior publication and will not jeopardise consideration; authors should disclose the preprint, with DOI and licence, at submission |
| Under review | Yes | The same page says preprints may be posted at any time during the peer review process |
| Post-acceptance (AAM) | Yes, with embargo | For subscription-route articles the accepted manuscript may go on a personal website immediately on acceptance and into an institutional or funder repository after 12 months (Springer hybrid and subscription journals row). Embargo: 12 months, the publisher's figure for this portfolio |
| Version of Record | Only through the gold route | Immediate open access to the version of record is available through the open-access route (how-to-publish page) |

## Format

> Source for every row: the journal's submission-guidelines page, https://link.springer.com/journal/799/submission-guidelines (read 2026-11-23), unless another page is named.

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Article types accepted** | The guidelines page lists no article-type menu. OpenAlex types for the window: 119 articles, 13 editorials, 5 errata, 1 review; the home page labels items "OriginalPaper" (https://link.springer.com/journal/799). The aims page lists "Artificial Intelligence for Digital Libraries", "Data Analytics", "Information Access and Retrieval" and "Human-Centered and Societal Aspects" among core areas (https://link.springer.com/journal/799/aims-and-scope) |
| **Word limit** | No word limit. Length is stated in pages: "Submissions, initial as well as final, are expected to be between 10 and 30 pages when formatted according to the two-column LaTeX template" |
| **Word limit negotiability** | Blank. Not stated |
| **Abstract limit** | Structured abstract of 150 to 250 words with Purpose, Methods, Results and Conclusion sections; 4 to 6 keywords |
| **Reference limit** | No cap stated. Numbered citations in square brackets, an ordered numbered list, DOIs as full links where available |
| **Supplementary material** | Allowed: electronic multimedia and other supplementary files published online with the article; datasets should be archived in repositories where possible |
| **Figure/Table limits** | No count limit. Tables numbered with Arabic numerals and captions; figures supplied electronically, vector graphics preferably EPS, halftones TIFF; online colour is free and print colour is charged |
| **Style / submission format** | LaTeX is the stated preference (Springer Nature template, "[iicol]" option, source files plus compiled PDF); Word is also accepted; decimal headings with at most three levels; footnotes, not endnotes; incomplete source files mean the article is not reviewed; Statements and Declarations (competing interests) required or the submission is returned as incomplete |

### Orientation

> Counts come from OpenAlex works of this source dated 2021-11-23 to 2026-11-23 (138 records of all types; 77 have an abstract, 68 of the 119 articles among them). Crossref's abstracts for the same DOIs add none (71 records, all already in OpenAlex), so 61 records, of which 51 are articles, have no abstract anywhere I could read, and every count below is a lower bound over a small base. A keyword counts when its regular expression (case-insensitive, listed in the regex table in AI-Research Notes) matches title plus abstract. Shares use the 77 records with abstracts as denominator. ### Framing Requirements

- **Mandatory framing?** A scope condition is stated: the journal "examines the theory and practice of creation, acquisition, organization, management, preservation, dissemination, discovery, access, and use of digital information via global networking", covering all aspects of digital libraries (aims page, https://link.springer.com/journal/799/aims-and-scope, read 2026-11-23).
- **What kind of engagement?** Digital-library framing: the aims page lists core areas (architectures, collections, curation and preservation, metadata, interoperability, web archiving, evaluation, electronic records, data provenance) plus AI for digital libraries, FAIR and CARE principles, data analytics, information access and retrieval, human-centred and societal aspects, and emerging trends. It encourages "both foundational theories and applied innovations".
- **Article type and length**: 10 to 30 pages in the two-column LaTeX template, structured abstract of 150 to 250 words (see Format).
- **Special-issue framing seen**: the open JCDL 2026 special issue takes extended conference papers under three themes (LLM-augmented discovery of large collections; trust, quality and integrity in AI-driven digital library systems; equity, access and the human experience) and asks for at least 30% new material (https://link.springer.com/collections/bddbbehaba); earlier calls are listed in Publication Frequency.
- **Consequences of ignoring it**: Blank. No page states what happens to out-of-scope submissions, and no desk-rejection data exists (SciRev: 1 review, https://scirev.org/journal/international-journal-on-digital-libraries/).

### Methodological Preferences

> Counts are records of this source dated 2021-11-23 to 2026-11-23 (OpenAlex: 138 records, 77 with an abstract) whose title or abstract matches the regex named in the regex table (AI-Research Notes). Shares use 77 as denominator, so each hit is worth 1.3 points and the scores are low-confidence. Scoring convention of this research pass (its own, not an external standard): share 0 = 0; under 1% = 1; 1-5% = 2; over 5% = 3; 4-5 only with a cited editorial statement together with a clearly dominant count. Scores measure how often a method appears, not how a reviewer would judge it.

| Method | Receptiveness (0-5) | Evidence |

| Quantitative experimental | 3 | experiments or user studies 13 (16.9%); surveys 11 (14.3%); "quantitative" 3 (3.9%). The aims page lists "Evaluation methodologies and user studies for DL systems" (https://link.springer.com/journal/799/aims-and-scope) |
| Qualitative interviews | 3 | interviews 6 (7.8%); "qualitative" 5 (6.5%) |
| Autoethnography | 2 | Ethnography or autoethnography terms 1 (1.3%) (the regex does not separate the two) |

| Mixed methods | 2 | "mixed methods" 2 (2.6%) |

| Machine learning / language-model methods (added row) | 4 | 24 (31.2%), a clearly dominant count, and an editorial statement: the aims page has a section "Artificial Intelligence for Digital Libraries" listing NLP, generative and agentic AI and explainable AI (https://link.springer.com/journal/799/aims-and-scope) |
| Dataset, benchmark and evaluation work (added row) | 3 | 37 (48.1%); the regex is broad, since "evaluation" and "datasets" occur in many abstracts |

### Practical Concerns

| Concern | Detail |
|---------|--------|
| **IRB requirement strictness** | Authors are requested to include sources of funding, competing interests, study-specific approval by the appropriate ethics committee for research involving humans or animals, and informed consent where human participants were involved; submissions without relevant declarations are returned as incomplete (https://link.springer.com/journal/799/submission-guidelines, read 2026-11-23). Few papers involve human participants by keyword (interviews 7.8%, surveys 14.3% of recent abstracts; see Methodological Preferences) |
| **Single-author acceptance** | Single-author papers are rare: 6 of 119 articles in the window (5.0%), against 54 with four or more authors (OpenAlex, retrieved 2026-11-23) |
| **Independent scholar friendliness** | An explicit rule exists: for authors who are temporarily unaffiliated the journal captures only city and country of residence, not an e-mail address unless requested; affiliations are otherwise institution, department, city, country (guidelines page, read 2026-11-23). No acceptance data |
| **Data transparency requirement** | A "type 1" research data policy: the journal encourages depositing data in a public repository; it does not mandate it (guidelines page, read 2026-11-23). Authors "should be prepared" to send raw data or records on request to verify results, except confidential data |
| **OPSEC compatibility** | Single-blind review: reviewers see author names, so no author anonymisation is expected (guidelines page). Preprints are encouraged by the publisher, so public preprints are compatible (https://www.springer.com/gp/editorial-policies/preprint-sharing) |
| **AI use** | Document LLM use in the Methods; LLMs are not authors; AI-assisted copy-editing need not be declared (AI Policy) |
| **Open access and cost** | Hybrid; no submission fee mentioned; APC GBP 2190, USD 3090 or EUR 2490 for the open-access route, paid after acceptance (Open Access) |
| **Originality and reuse** | The page says submission implies the work is unpublished and not under consideration elsewhere, and the integrity list says the work should be original; the journal may screen for plagiarism; expansions of earlier work need transparent reporting of re-used material, and invited authors of the JCDL special issue are asked to extend their conference paper by at least 30% (guidelines page; https://link.springer.com/collections/bddbbehaba) |

## Strategic Notes

> Each statement below follows from a fact recorded above and names it. Where the evidence does not support a statement, the field says so.

### Hard Blockers

- **Length format**: submissions, initial and final, are expected at 10 to 30 pages in the two-column LaTeX template (Format).
- **Source files**: manuscripts without a complete set of editable source files are not reviewed (Format).
- **Declarations**: submissions without the required Statements and Declarations (competing interests) are returned as incomplete; research with human participants needs ethics approval and consent statements (Practical Concerns).
- **Special-issue route**: invited authors in the JCDL 2026 special issue are asked to extend the conference paper by at least 30% and the extended submission goes through the standard review (Publication Frequency).

### Soft Tax

- **Time**: the publisher reports a 24-day median to first decision (Review Cycle Time); the one SciRev report (a special-issue paper) describes a 5.0-month first round and 5.5 months in total, which is a single data point.
- **Open access cost**: gold OA carries an APC of GBP 2190, USD 3090 or EUR 2490; green deposit of the accepted manuscript to a repository has a 12-month embargo, with immediate posting to a personal website (Open Access, Preprint Policy).
- **Not anonymised**: single-blind review means author identity is visible to reviewers (Peer Review).
- **Format**: LaTeX with the publisher's two-column template is the stated preference; the page-based limit rather than a word limit means reformatting for another venue (Format).

### Best Suited For

- Systems, collections and infrastructure work in digital libraries, with evaluation: datasets, benchmarks or evaluation wording appears in 48.1% of recent abstracts, and the aims page lists architectures, preservation, metadata and evaluation of digital library systems (Orientation, Framing Requirements).
- Machine-learning and language-model work applied to collections or scholarly documents: 31.2% of recent abstracts, with an AI section on the aims page and special-issue calls on the topic (Methodological Preferences).
- Extended versions of work first presented at the joint conferences: the journal runs special issues for JCDL, ICADL and TPDL with a 30% extension rule (Publication Frequency).
- Indigenous data governance and inclusive design in digital collections: named on the aims page and in a past special-issue call (Epistemological & Political Leanings).
- Team-authored papers: 54 of 119 articles in the window have four or more authors (Voice & Style).

### Not Recommended For

- Primarily theoretical or critical-social work with no systems or collections component: theory or conceptual wording is in 10.4% and critical or philosophical wording in 0% of recent abstracts (Methodological Preferences, Epistemological & Political Leanings). The counts show these forms are uncommon here, not that they are rejected, and rest on 77 abstracts.
- Sole authors: 6 of 119 articles are single-author (Practical Concerns).
- Authors needing a published acceptance rate or reviewer-quality evidence before choosing: neither exists on the pages read (Metrics, Reviewer Pool Characteristics).
- Authors needing double-blind review: the journal states single-blind (Peer Review).
